title: HarborGlass Fleet - intake scratchpad
body:
Context:
- Customer: HarborGlass Fleet (vehicle glass replacement and fleet ops)
- Use case: in-vehicle incident triage + automated claim summaries + parts recommendation. They want low-latency on-vehicle inference with occasional cloud fallback for heavy workloads.
- Contact: Marco Ruiz (CTO), Lina Park (Head of Ops)

Call notes (2025-01-13 discovery):
- Intro: short background, they're migrating from an on-prem rules engine + batch OCR pipeline to a realtime LLM + vision assisted workflow.
- Primary goals: reduce field tech decision time (target: 2–3 min -> under 30s), auto-generate repair estimate drafts, tag parts and stock locations.
- SLO targets mentioned: P95 latency < 250ms for local inference path (when on-vehicle compute available), cloud fallback P95 < 1.5s, throughput: expected 20 concurrent vehicles per region initially, burst to 200 during peak events.
- Privacy/regulatory: they process PII (driver names, license plates). Need at-rest encryption, KMS, and option for customer-managed keys.
- Network constraints: vehicles have intermittent connectivity; must operate offline for up to 12 hours.
- Model/quality: want high factuality on parts recommendation (precision prioritized over recall). They asked about retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with parts DB and serial-number lookup.
- Ops expectations: want a runbook for fallback logic and ability to pin model versions. Also ask for token-cost estimate for pilot (3 months).

Technical requirements (collected):
- On-vehicle: small quantized model (4-bit) with ~6-7B parameter equivalent that fits on a single edge GPU (Jetson Orin or similar).
- Fallback: Redwood hosted API + Dedicated pool in us-west for low-latency fallback.
- Data residency: US-only for now, possible EU region next year.
- Security: SOC2 is must; need integration with their Azure AD for SSO + SAML for console access.
- Audit/logging: full request/response logging for debug for first 90 days, then sampling. Must support redaction of PII fields before retention.
- Model ops: version pinning, canary rollout for model updates, metric hooks to monitor precision on parts-lookup.

Gotchas / risks we flagged (notes-to-self):
- On-vehicle compute spec vague -> get exact GPU model and memory. "Jetson" often means lots of variants.
- Parts DB lookups: need latency budget allocation; RAG with local snapshot might be required to meet 250ms goal.
- Offline mode: how to handle KV cache/embedding DB sync? Strategy: periodic delta sync + LRU eviction. Need to recommend frequency (every 6–12 hours) and fallback logic.
- Cost sensitivity: small fleet but high per-token sensitivity because of long conversations per van. Provide batching + cache suggestions.
- Telemetry volume: storing full request/response for 20->200 vehicles will be expensive; propose sampling + structured summaries.

Open questions to follow up (action items):
- A1: Marco to confirm exact edge hardware (GPU model + memory + OS image). (Due: 2025-01-21)
- A2: Lina to share sample parts DB (CSV) and expected query patterns (search by SKU, visual match, serial). (Due: 2025-01-20)
- A3: Ask legal if they require data residency for backups (are backups to be US-only?). (Owner: Priya)
- A4: Clarify retention policy for logs and whether PII redaction rules are already defined. (Owner: Evan)
- A5: Request example incident transcript and current decision-tree rules to estimate token count per flow. (Owner: Samira)

Pilot proposal sketch (for internal review, not sent):
- Phase 0 (Prep): gather hardware + sample DB + transcripts. 2 weeks.
- Phase 1 (Edge POC): deploy quantized 6B model on 2 vehicles, local RAG with snapshot of parts DB, measure P95 local latency and throughput. 3 weeks.
- Phase 2 (Hybrid fallback): integrate Redwood hosted fallback in us-west, implement cache + KV sync, telemetry hooks. 4 weeks.
- Phase 3 (Scale & Security): SAML + KMS integration, retention + redact pipeline, SLA doc and runbooks. 3 weeks.
- Target pilot length: 8–10 weeks total.

Preliminary sizing / cost notes (very rough):
- Edge: cost depends on their hardware. If using Orin X with 32GB, can probably host a 6B quant; otherwise may need 3B + model distillation.
- Hosted tokens: average tokens/interaction estimate TBD; rough calc: 500 tokens per incident * 20 vehicles * 3 incidents/day * 30 days = 900k tokens/month baseline. Multiply by cost-per-token. Need to put concrete numbers in proposal.

Suggested next steps (to send in follow-up email):
- Send concise pilot scope + ask list (hardware spec, parts CSV, example transcripts).
- Schedule 30m tech deep-dive with infra + privacy SME: invite Evan and Samira.
- Offer an architecture sketch: Edge-first with periodic RAG sync + hosted fallback + dedicated pool in us-west.

Notes / scratch thoughts (quick fragments):
- Could use prefix caching for repeated vehicular forms (old VINs, common part names) -> reduces token usage.
- If parts DB is normalized and small (<5k rows) we could embed locally and do ANN lookup on-device (fast).
- For PII redaction: ship a lightweight pre-filter on vehicle to mask plates before sync.
- SLO trade: accept slightly higher P99 on offline-only scenarios; keep P95 tight for online local inference.

Draft email outline to Marco/Lina (send after A1/A2 received):
- Quick thanks + recap of goals (reduce decision time, offline-first, secure)
- Attach pilot scope + ask list and timeline
- Propose tech deep-dive slot w/ options for next week

Quick personal TODO (Priya):
- Fill cost model spreadsheet with token assumptions once Samira has sample transcript.
- Draft initial architecture diagram for the deep-dive (use figma template).
- Confirm whether Dedicated pool costs can be shown as monthly commit vs burst pricing for them.

End of notes.

-- Priya (raw scratchpad)
